# Summary of the UK Independence Party (UKIP) Manifesto

## Core Ideology and Mission

The UK Independence Party, founded in 1993, presents itself as a moderate, mainstream party dedicated to restoring British sovereignty through withdrawal from the European Union. The party frames the EU as a "confidence trick" that has betrayed the 1975 referendum promise of a simple common market, instead creating a centralised, bureaucratic, unaccountable superstate that threatens British freedom, democracy, and prosperity.

## Economic Vision

UKIP champions genuine free trade and globalisation, arguing that EU membership actually restricts Britain's trading potential through external tariff barriers. The party emphasises Britain's position as the world's fourth-largest economy, head of the Commonwealth, and a natural global trading power held back by EU over-regulation.

Central to their economic platform is the "Independence Dividend"—approximately £20 billion annually from ceasing EU budget contributions (£8.5-11 billion) plus economic gains from deregulation. This windfall would fund increased pensions, NHS spending, defence, policing, education, and fuel tax reductions.

The party advocates aggressive deregulation, particularly for small businesses, viewing EU regulations as job-destroying burdens favouring large corporations. They oppose the euro permanently, seeing monetary union as fundamentally about political control rather than economic benefit.

## Public Services and Welfare

UKIP proposes restoring traditional NHS management through the "matron system," increasing nurses' pay, and reducing bureaucracy. In education, they support academic selection, streaming, traditional teaching methods, reduced class sizes, and freedom from "politically-correct" curricula and EU propaganda. State pensions would increase by £5 weekly.

## Constitutional and Legal Framework

The party positions itself as defenders of British common law, trial by jury, presumption of innocence, and parliamentary sovereignty against EU legal harmonisation through "Corpus Juris." They propose a new Bill of Rights preventing future sovereignty transfers and oppose regionalisation as EU-driven balkanisation.

## Immigration and Social Policy

UKIP advocates firm but humane immigration controls determined solely by the British Parliament, supporting skills-based immigration and expedited asylum processing while criticising EU open borders.
